obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: A Cyber Security Incident that compromised or disrupted a high or medium impact BES Cyber System (EMS, Substations P, R, K) or its EACMS, as determined under the R1 Part 1.2 process
deadline: Within 1 hour after the determination; initial notice includes, to the extent known, functional impact, attack vector, and level of intrusion
notify: E-ISAC and CISA (NCCIC successor), unless prohibited by law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - high and medium impact BES Cyber Systems and EACMS
clock_starts: Time of the documented determination by the CIP Senior Manager delegate on duty

obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 attempt to compromise notification
trigger: A Cyber Security Incident determined, using the R1 Part 1.2.1 criteria, to be an attempt to compromise a high or medium impact BES Cyber System or its EACMS (for example, scanning of the TCC Electronic Access Point from a compromised host)
deadline: By the end of the next calendar day after the determination

trigger: New or changed information about functional impact, attack vector, or level of intrusion
deadline: Within 7 calendar days of determining the new or changed information
clock_starts: Determination of new or changed attribute information

obligation: Low impact Reportable Cyber Security Incident notice
trigger: A Reportable Cyber Security Incident at one of the 143 low impact substations
deadline: CIP-003-9 sets no fixed time; it requires the determination and then notification unless prohibited by law. Company target: within 1 hour of the determination (POL-03 4.4)

citation: Form DOE-417 criteria 1-9; Federal Energy Administration Act of 1974 sec. 13(b); OMB 1901-0288
trigger: Includes criterion 2 (Reportable Cyber Security Incident), 3 (cyber event that is not a Reportable Cyber Security Incident but causes interruptions of electrical system operations), 6 (uncontrolled loss of 300 MW or more of firm load for more than 15 minutes from a single incident), and 7 (firm load shedding of 100 MW or more under emergency operational policy)
deadline: Within 1 hour of the incident. If operations are critically affected, telephone notice to the DOE Operations Center is acceptable pending the written form
notify: DOE CESER (DOE-417 online system); the filer can select sharing with NERC, the E-ISAC, and CISA on line W
owner: Director, Distribution Control Center (files from the DCC checklist); Director, NERC Compliance

trigger: Includes criterion 11 (cyber event that could potentially impact electric power system adequacy or reliability) and 12 (loss of electric service to more than 50,000 customers for 1 hour or more), when no Emergency Alert criterion applies
deadline: Within 6 hours of the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 1.95 million meters, so criterion 12 is easily met

trigger: A Cyber Security Incident that was an attempt to compromise a high or medium impact BES Cyber System or its EACMS, when no Emergency Alert or Normal Report criterion applies
deadline: By the end of the next calendar day after the determination of the attempted cyber compromise (Form DOE-417 and its instructions, OMB 1901-0288); sharing through line W with the E-ISAC and CISA can satisfy CIP-008 reporting
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - added to the DCC and TCC checklists by 2026-10-31 (P03 G-152)

trigger: For example, damage or destruction of a Facility from suspected intentional human action, physical threats to a Facility or control center, uncontrolled loss of 500 MW or more from inverter-based resources for more than 30 minutes at a common point of interconnection (criterion 27, added in the 2024 revision), or complete loss of monitoring or control at a staffed BES control center for 30 minutes or more, when no higher criterion applies
deadline: By the later of 24 hours after recognizing the incident or the end of the next business day (4 p.m. local time)

citation: Form DOE-417 instructions (Update Report; Final Report)
trigger: Significant new information; every filed report
deadline: Update when significant information becomes available; final report (Schedule 1 and all of Schedule 2) within 72 hours of the incident unless an interim update was provided

trigger: Attachment 1 events for DP, TO, and TOP, for example uncontrolled loss of firm load of 300 MW or more for 15 minutes or more from a single incident (entities with prior-year peak of 3,000 MW or more), damage or destruction of a Facility from intentional human action, or complete loss of monitoring or control at a staffed BES control center for 30 minutes or more
deadline: By the later of 24 hours after recognizing the event met a threshold or the end of the next business day (4 p.m. local time)
notify: NERC (systemawareness@nerc.net) and the parties in the Operating Plan (Reliability Coordinator, Regional Entity, law enforcement where relevant). A DOE-417 form may be submitted instead when DOE-417 is also required
clock_starts: Recognition that the event met a threshold

obligation: Operational coordination with the Reliability Coordinator and Balancing Authority
citation: TOP operating obligations and the RC procedures (operational, not a cyber reporting rule)
trigger: Any event that affects transmission monitoring, control, or load served from the BES
deadline: Immediately by the TCC, as the RC procedures require
notify: Reliability Coordinator; Balancing Authority; neighboring TOPs

trigger: Any cybersecurity incident that may be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery
notify: Disclosure committee (internal decision, recorded with date, time, and basis)

trigger: Determination that a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
citation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 (national security or public safety delay)
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines that disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay only for the period the Attorney General specifies
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines (plausible for a grid attack)

citation: Reg S-K Item 106 (17 CFR 229.106); Form 10-K Item 1C
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the Form 10-K

citation: Company insider trading policy (not a regulatory deadline)
trigger: Severity-1 incident with possible material impact
deadline: At declaration for those with knowledge; committee-wide when it convenes

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
trigger: Breach of personal information as each state defines it (for example, name with SSN or account number from the CIS; portal credentials)
deadline: Varies by state; follow the shortest applicable clock
applies_at_this_tier: Only if CIS, portal, or other personal information is accessed. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside
clock_starts: Determination of the breach under each state law

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: State thresholds for regulator notice
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorneys general or regulators where required

trigger: State thresholds (counts of affected residents)
deadline: Varies by state

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. OMS names, addresses, and phone numbers alone are not listed data elements; counsel decides whether medical-priority flags combined with names count as medical information under the statute, and whether premise map locations count as geolocation information
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (15-day extension on good cause, individual notice only)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information as defined is accessed
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (no extension)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Florida residents are affected

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Only if more than 1,000 individuals are notified
clock_starts: Decision to notify more than 1,000 individuals

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice: vendors to the company (worked example)
trigger: A vendor holding customer personal information (CIS hosting services, bill print, collection agency) discovers a breach
deadline: Within 10 days after the vendor determines the breach; company contracts require 72 hours

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice: the company to SL-1 client utilities (worked example)
trigger: A breach of SL-1 client utilities customer data held by the company as their third-party agent
deadline: Within 10 days after the company determines the breach; client agreements require 24 hours for any security incident
notify: Each affected client utility, which then decides on its own notices

trigger: Any security incident affecting the Utility Services platform or client data
deadline: Within 24 hours of confirmation

trigger: Any security incident affecting fleet charging services or client data
deadline: Within 48 hours of confirmation

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any payment to an extortionist
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Voluntary report to the FBI and CISA
trigger: Any intrusion into OT
deadline: As soon as practicable (company target: same day; usually through the CIP-008 notice to CISA)

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging response vendors

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated pipeline
deadline: No later than 72 hours after identification
notify: CISA Central; CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company operates no pipelines

trigger: Cyber attack on a power reactor licensee digital assets
deadline: 1 hour / 4 hours / 8 hours depending on event
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no NRC reactor license

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Discovery of covered telecommunications equipment or services in performance of a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts identified; recheck if contracts are awarded

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Discovery of a covered article in performance of a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts identified; recheck if contracts are awarded
